title: Firstmate's no-mistakes status reads time out in its partial clones: a missing pipeline head starts a lazy fetch that costs 30 s of CPU, and the 10 s bound leaves the git child running (10-17)
description:
Measured on the laptop 10-17 by ep-laptop.

What happens: Firstmate's GSP clone (~/dev/firstmate/projects/groove-sight-platform, blob:none partial clone, origin is the promisor; 354 of 357 packs are promisor packs, 10.6M objects) serves every treehouse slot. When a no-mistakes run's pipeline head is not in the clone (the gate made fix commits that were not pushed yet), `no-mistakes axi status` checks it with `git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}` (no-mistakes internal/branchsync/sync.go:2717 objectExists, upstream kunchenguid/no-mistakes, still so at d228adb). In a partial clone a missing object starts a lazy fetch: origin answers "not our ref" twice, then git spends about 30 s of one core before it gives up.

Baseline, slot ~/.treehouse/groove-sight-platform-5f20d7/48/groove-sight-platform:
- `no-mistakes axi status`: real 38.84 s, user 30.66 s.
- the same command with GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1: real 0.43 s, and the same full status (gate, findings, next action).
- `git cat-file -e b1b247df...^{commit}`: 31.46 s, 29.82 s user. With GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1: 0.02 s.

Who calls it: fm-crew-state.sh, through fm_nm_run_bounded (bin/fm-nm-run-lib.sh) with a 10 s bound. In a 10-minute process sample, Firstmate made 6 of these probes for crews ac-jr3ip, gsp-novcw and gsp-seat-watchers (heads 3cad6a62, b1b247df, fed277a6). The sample can miss short ones. Two results:
1. The status read always times out, so Firstmate reads those three crews' gate as "daemon, timeout, or unreachable" every tick, never their real gate state. ac-jr3ip is Chip's P0 review-gate restore.
2. The timeout stops no-mistakes but not its git child. The child moves to launchd (ppid 1) and keeps one core busy for about 20 s more. That is about 0.3 core all the time while those heads stay missing.

fm-teardown.sh:2217 uses the same runner (NM_TEARDOWN_TIMEOUT), and fm-teardown.sh:1553 and fm-review-diff.sh:142 make the same bare probe in $WT. fm-role-lib.sh:261 already uses GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 for its own probe, so the pattern is known in Firstmate.

The fix (Firstmate's code, gsp-agent/firstmate):
(a) fm_nm_run_bounded runs no-mistakes with GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1. A status read never needs to fetch from origin: the missing head is in the gate repo, not on origin. Do the same at fm-teardown.sh:1553/1557 and fm-review-diff.sh:142, where the next line already fetches the PR head explicitly.
(b) fm_nm_bounded's timeout stops the whole process tree, so a bounded call leaves no orphan.
Not here: an upstream no-mistakes change to objectExists (git --no-lazy-fetch). It is outward, in a third-party repo, and (a) removes the cost on this machine.

Done:
- With the change live in Firstmate's checkout, in a slot whose pipeline head is absent, fm_nm_run_bounded <slot> 10 axi status returns the gate in under 1 s (baseline: timeout at 10 s).
- A 10-minute sample on the laptop (pgrep -f "git cat-file -e" with ancestry; ep-laptop's sampler is /tmp/ep-laptop-notes/catch-catfile.sh 600) shows 0 cat-file probes left under launchd from fm-crew-state (baseline 6).
- fm-crew-state.sh for ac-jr3ip reads the crew's real gate state, not timeout.

comments.author: ep-laptop
comments.text:
ep-laptop (seat d5021d8e): the cost has grown since the bead was filed, and a second caller shows up.

Rate, sampled every 5 s (sampler: /tmp/ep-laptop-notes/catch-catfile-slow.sh <seconds>):
- 15 lazy-fetch `git cat-file -e` runs in the last 10 min, and 26 in the 15 min before that. Baseline at filing: 6 in 10 min.
- 5 missing heads now (dbf9b03a x6, b1b247df x3, fed277a6 x3, 8f139d0d x2, 163abe81 x1), up from 3.
- At ~30 s CPU each, that is about 0.75 of a core all the time.

Callers in the 10-min sample:
- 12 of 15 are Firstmate's `timeout 10 no-mistakes axi status` (fm_nm_run_bounded): fix (a) covers these.
- 3 of 15 are a Muse worker (crew gsp-faov2) running bare `no-mistakes axi status` in its slot every ~5 min. One more in the earlier sample was a worker's `no-mistakes axi respond --step review --action fix`. Fix (a) does not reach these: they come from the worker's own shell, not fm-nm-run-lib.sh.
- So done check 2 ("0 cat-file probes left under launchd from fm-crew-state") can pass while workers still pay ~30 s per call. Their calls finish rather than orphan (no timeout), so they cost CPU and wall time but leave nothing under launchd.

Queue: 32nd of 51 waiting for agent-config's 3 PM slots on the starter's last pass. Kept at P1: about one core of 16 with 40% idle is waste, not an emergency.

comments.text: ep-laptop reading, 10-19 00:55 CT: the same lazy-fetch orphans now also come from Firstmate's GSP treehouse slots, beyond ac-jr3ip's clone. There were three `git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}` processes at once under launchd (ppid 1), 31-43% CPU each, about 1 core together. Their cwds were ~/.treehouse/groove-sight-platform-5f20d7/{1,28,48}/groove-sight-platform; all three are blob:none promisor clones, and slot 48's .fm-slot-owner reads task=gsp-novcw. The remote does not hold the object (ce797d93…: "upload-pack: not our ref"), so each check pays a fetch that cannot succeed. Load 65, CPU idle 4% at the time. A 3-minute sample afterward caught only 2 new ones, so it comes in bursts. Next reader: probing a missing sha in these clones (`git cat-file -t`) itself starts the fetch, so read the cwd and the slot owner instead.

comments.author: ep-laptop
comments.text:
ep-laptop reading, 10-19 afternoon. Why the same probes kept coming back: the four pipeline heads being probed (e26952cf, fa56282a, ce620a9b, 96b75814; GSP treehouse slots 13, 28, 48) exist only in no-mistakes' local gate repo (~/.no-mistakes/repos/65c1217461b7.git), not on GitHub. So each probe's lazy fetch from origin could never succeed and was retried every poll. Before: 3 orphans found and stopped, then 7 new ones within 3 minutes on those four shas.
One-off data repair, no mechanism added: fetched the four commits from the gate repo into the shared GSP object store (/Users/dalecarman/dev/firstmate/projects/groove-sight-platform/.git) with `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git fetch --no-tags --no-write-fetch-head no-mistakes <shas>` (2.6 s, objects only, no refs), and stopped the 7 orphans. After: a 10-minute sample at 10 s showed 0 orphan cat-file probes. CPU stayed under 1% idle, so these were not the whole load.
It returns with the next pipeline head that is absent from a slot's clone. The cause is still this bead's fix (GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH and a tree-killing bound), and the repair suggests a second option for the PM: fetch the missing head from the no-mistakes remote rather than from origin.
